body:
In case-insensitive mode this allocates a new lowercased Vec on every lookup (`candidate.path.to_ascii_lowercase()`), which can significantly reduce the benefit of the literal fast path. You can avoid allocations for the common case where the candidate path is already ASCII-lowercase by first attempting a direct lookup with the original bytes and only allocating a lowercased copy on miss.

This issue also appears on line 767 of the same file.

In case-insensitive mode this allocates a new lowercased Vec for every basename lookup (`candidate.basename.to_ascii_lowercase()`). To keep the basename-literal fast path cheap, consider trying a direct lookup with the original bytes first and only allocating a lowercased copy on miss.

This issue also appears on line 819 of the same file.

This introduces new routing logic and new match behavior in `GlobSet::new` for case-insensitive `Literal`/`BasenameLiteral` strategies, but there don’t appear to be GlobSet-level tests that exercise a case-insensitive *pure literal* (e.g. `GlobBuilder::new("FOO").case_insensitive(true)`) or a case-insensitive basename-literal (e.g. `**/FOO`). Adding a small unit test in `lib.rs`’s test module would help prevent regressions in the new strategy split logic.
